My starting routine
The same 4 steps for every question
READ
Read the rule and the domain written after it.
FIND
Find the turning point, if there is one, and the end points.
SKETCH
Sketch only the part of the graph the domain allows.
WRITE
Write the range using f(x), not x.

6
Try one first, with Dyna
Find the range of  f(x) = (x − 2)2 + 3  for x ≥ 0.
Range
Before you open a hint, write your plan in one line:
Hint 1 · Echo
Say it in your own words: “A square, plus 3. Only x ≥ 0 is allowed.”
Hint 2 · Roots
Ask why a square helps: (x − 2)2 is never negative. When is it exactly 0, and is that x allowed?
Hint 3 · Translator
Make a table for x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and look for the smallest output.
YOUR TURN
Is there a smallest output? Is there a largest? Write the range.
Use the hints one at a time. Try on your own before you read the next one.
Before you start
Read Section 1.2 of the coursebook: the definition of a function, domain and range, and Worked examples 1 and 2.
Challenge ahead
Q 7 turns the curve upside down: a hill instead of a valley. Q 8 brings in a square root.
